purpose: Partition the existing F1 observer contract into claims that are closed in the solver component basis and claims that require a producer-to-world orientation record. This additive sidecar does not change the consumed v1/v2 contract or any tolerance.

component_space_native.meaning: The stored x/y/z component tuple, typed role, native header mass, component-space weighted COM/velocity/KE, and exact decoded saved time may be reported in solver-component coordinates when the source XML/control, role mapping, native producer proof, and source time convention are joined.
preconditions: same producer storage convention and component labels are source-bound
fluid/fixed/moving roles are disjoint and identity-checked
native header mass is used for weighted quantities; XML mass is not a native fallback
time comes from decoded seconds/RunPARTs, never frame index
the report says component-space and makes no physical-world direction claim
component_space_native.reason: These preconditions establish a bounded data-integrity/diagnostic scope, not continuum truth, integration error, output error, or external validation.

examples: cross-case comparison whose axes are physical rather than solver-component axes
required_evidence: producer writer/case source record for the solver-to-world transform
exact source SHA/stat and binary receipt/request join
the transform is tied to the same XML geometry, gravity, and control inputs
world_frame_physical.reason: JPartDataBi4 stores ordered component arrays but the current small writer/dump evidence has no producer-to-world transform record. Gravity [0,0,-9.81] is an input expressed in the solver basis and does not independently prove that basis is physically oriented.

evidence: JSph.cpp:3031-3034 defines TimeStep [s] as physical simulation time and runtime [s]
JSph.cpp:786-787 reads TimeMax and TimeOut as run/output times
JSphGpuSimple_ker.cu:161-163 computes displacement as velocity*dt plus acceleration*dt^2/2 componentwise
JSphGpuSimple_ker.cu:300-302 computes displacement as velocity*dt componentwise
JSphGpuSimple_ker.cu:443-445 computes predictor/corrector displacement from velocity*dt
F1 XML gravity carries units_comment=m/s^2 and position geometry is metres
velocity.scope: This closes the SI time/velocity convention in the actual solver update chain; it does not close the producer-to-world orientation or a physical-world velocity claim.

required_join: the three actual generated XML/Def source records and unchanged control parameters
ROOT207 proof/request/receipt identity and SHA (proof payload is not read by this sidecar)
native header Dp/MassFluid/MassBound and role/Idp evidence from the guarded observer
actual decoded saved timestamp/RunPARTs evidence for every compared row

stages.name: same-time component arithmetic
stages.operation: Compare only rows whose decoded saved times are equal within the pre-registered timestamp equality rule; use native mass-weighted fluid COM, velocity, and KE, with fixed/moving groups excluded.

stages.name: asynchronous saved-time separation
stages.operation: For each requested physical query, report actual lower/upper frame IDs, times, bracket width, and whether an exact native row exists. Keep field differences, time misalignment, integration effects, output sampling effects, and spatial-grid differences as separate UNKNOWN components.
stages.credit: metadata/diagnostic only; a bracket is not a field-error bound

stages.name: world-frame extension
stages.operation: Do not promote component results to gravity/world direction until a producer-to-world orientation source record is joined.

mass_scope.rule: These sample masses are recorded for diagnostics only; their differences are not a truth estimate and cannot replace the unresolved continuum-owner contract.

f1_s2_next_minimum_task.frozen_tolerance_policy: Use the already consumed F1 task contract and its tolerances unchanged; do not widen a gate or infer truth from a neighboring grid.

world_orientation_status.why_not_a_global_prerequisite: A component-space native record is still a well-defined ordered tuple even when its physical-world orientation is unknown. Orientation is a gate for world-frame interpretation, not for every storage, role, mass, COM, velocity-unit, or saved-time diagnostic.
known_source_limits: JPartDataBi4.cpp creates Idp/Posd-or-Pos/Vel/Rhop arrays without a world transform
JPartDataBi4.h exposes component array getters, not a world orientation
bi4_dump.cpp is a read-only storage dump and does not assign physical axes
gravity XML values alone do not independently calibrate the producer axis
